biography:
Alex Riberas, a name whispered with a mix of admiration and trepidation in the paddock, hails from the sun-baked streets of Valencia, Spain. Growing up amidst the roar of motorbikes, Alex's passion was ignited early. He began tearing up local go-kart tracks at the age of 10, his aggressive style quickly earning him a reputation. His breakthrough came unexpectedly when a scout from Maximum Orange spotted him overtaking three karts in a single corner at the regional championships. 

Signed to Maximum Orange's young driver program, Riberas quickly ascended the ranks, showcasing a raw talent that bordered on recklessness. He secured a surprise victory at the junior world series in his second year, a moment celebrated with paella and fiery flamenco at his family's restaurant back home. However, his impetuous nature often led to costly mistakes, hindering his progress towards the pinnacle of motorsport. 

After a brief, unremarkable stint with Aston Martin's junior squad, where his aggressive style clashed with the team's focus on precision, Riberas found himself adrift. Now in his late thirties, the fire still burns, but the opportunities are dwindling. He currently competes in less prestigious GT series, clinging to the hope of a late-career resurgence, even as the younger generation eclipses him.

Despite facing setbacks, Riberas remains a respected figure, a reminder of the raw, untamed talent that once promised so much, but ultimately never reached its full potential.
drivingStyle: Riberas is a visceral driver, relying more on instinct than calculated strategy. He attacks corners with unrelenting aggression, often braking later and carrying more speed through the apex than his competitors deem possible. While this approach can yield spectacular results, it also makes him prone to errors, particularly in tire management. He struggles to adapt to changing track conditions, often sticking stubbornly to his initial setup, even when it's clearly not working. In high-pressure situations, Riberas tends to become even more aggressive, either pulling off a miraculous overtake or crashing out spectacularly.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision at the 24 Hours of Le Mans, where Bellini accused Riberas of reckless driving.
A clash of personalities and driving styles, with Dubois, a meticulous and precise driver, often criticizing Riberas's aggressive and unpredictable approach.
Riberas and Tanaka engaged in a fierce battle for the GT World Championship title, marked by several on-track incidents and heated exchanges in the media.

quirks: Always wears a lucky red bracelet given to him by his grandmother before every race.
Refuses to eat anything green on race day, believing it brings bad luck.
Listens to a specific flamenco track on repeat in the hour leading up to the race to pump himself up.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. I race to win, or I crash trying."
careerHighlight: Winning the Junior World Series Championship against all odds after a daring last-lap overtake, cementing his status as a rising star.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the Spanish Grand Prix, in front of his home crowd, due to an overly aggressive move.
